title: Policy sandbox for safe surge scaling and throughput guardrails
creator: Jared Kim
description:
Goal: Design and implement a "policy sandbox" component inside the Dedicated autoscaling engine that allows teams to author, simulate, and safely roll out surge scaling policies tied to throughput guarantees. The sandbox will validate policies against safety limits, simulate historical traffic (prefix-based replay), and provide a canary rollout path that enforces hard caps and graceful draining for stateful model workers.

Scope:
- Policy language for target metrics, scaling algorithm selection, and safety limits.
- Simulation and replay tooling for policy validation.
- Runtime enforcement layer with hard safety guards (min/max nodes, surge window limits, cooldowns).
- Canary and staged rollout support integrated with Console and rollouts APIs.

Non-goals: automated ML-driven policy tuning (future), full UI polish for sandbox (MVP will be API/CLI + basic Console integration).

Background: Dedicated customers require predictable throughput guarantees while keeping unit cost low. Current autoscaler supports simple target-tracking and step policies but lacks a safe validation path for aggressive surge behaviors (e.g., sudden tokens/sec spike driven by batch jobs). We need a formalized policy sandbox that prevents catastrophic scale-offs and respects KV cache affinity and stateful model drain semantics.
design_summary:
Target metrics: tokens_per_sec (cluster & pool), p95_latency, queue_length, GPU_utilization, active_sessions.

Scaling algorithms supported in sandbox MVP: target-tracking PID-like controller (tunable proportional/integral terms), exponential step-up with capped ramp, schedule-based surge windows, and conservative reactive policy (threshold + hold).

Safety limits: global and per-pool min/max replicas, max_surge_rate (percent increase per minute), cooldown_seconds, max_concurrent_scale_actions, drain_timeout_seconds (for KV/cache and in-flight sequences), and fallback_model_routes. Policies must declare required affinity hints for cache locality and whether horizontal scaling is safe for the model (stateless vs stateful).

Policy language: YAML-based declarative schema that expresses metric sources, target thresholds, algorithm and parameters, safety limits, and rollout config. Example: metric: tokens_per_sec; algorithm: step-ramp; step_size: 20%; max_surge_rate: 40%; cooldown: 120s; drain_timeout: 30s.

Validation & simulation: Use 7d historical traffic slices and synthetic spike patterns. Simulation outputs: expected replica-time series, worst-case queue depth, KV cache miss rate delta, estimated token-cost delta, and SLA violation probability. Policies that show >1% SLA violation probability or >50% cache-miss regression are rejected by the sandbox unless overridden with explicit risk acknowledgment.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Latency vs cost: aggressive surge reduces tail latency but increases idle GPU time and costs.
- Cache affinity: scaling across racks may increase cold KV cache misses; we mitigate via affinity hints and gradual ramping.
- Stateful model draining: long drain time reduces effective capacity during scale-in. We cap scale-in rate and require explicit drain_timeout per model.
- Complexity: more knobs increases user configuration burden; mitigate by providing sane defaults and policy templates.
- Safety vs flexibility: strict validation prevents some high-performance policies; provide override path for verified SREs with audit logging.
rollout_plan:
MVP (sprint 1-2): implement YAML policy schema, local simulator (CLI), and enforcement stubs in autoscaler; integrate rollout APIs for canary.
Beta (sprint 3-4): integrate with Console UI, add 7d replay capability, and telemetry dashboards for policy behavior.
GA (release dedicated-2026.04): documentation, policy templates (steady-state, bursty-batch, latency-sensitive), SRE training, and opt-in for selected customers.

Canary strategy: 1) policy creation in sandbox -> 2) dry-run mode (simulation + no enforcement) -> 3) canary rollout to single pool with conservative caps -> 4) monitored autoscale for 24–72 hours -> 5) gradual expansion if metrics are stable. Metrics gating: p95 latency, tokens_per_sec throughput, average GPU utilization, cache-miss delta, error_rate.
acceptance_criteria: Policy YAML schema documented and validated by unit tests (schema tests passing)
Simulator can replay 7d historical traffic and produce replica-time series and cache-miss estimates
Enforcement layer honors max_surge_rate, cooldown_seconds, and min/max replica bounds at runtime
Canary rollout path exists and can be initiated via Console API; canary can be aborted automatically on SLA breach
Integration tests covering stateful model drain semantics (graceful termination within drain_timeout)
